avatar_brief: Woman 52-60, sitting on a closed toilet lid in a small bathroom with the cabinet open behind her, products visibly crowded on the shelves. No makeup, hair up. Delivery is deadpan and slightly self-mocking — she is indicting her own past spending, not lecturing the viewer.
hook: I counted. Eleven products, and nine of them are mostly water.
first_frame: Open bathroom cabinet crammed with bottles, shot straight on. Her hand is already reaching in to start pulling them out.

beats.vo: I counted. Eleven products, and nine of them are mostly water.
beats.visual: Cabinet open, she lifts out bottles one at a time and lines them on the sink.

beats.vo: That's what a light lotion is. Water, a thickener, and enough active to put on the front of the box.
beats.visual: She tips one bottle sideways — the lotion runs thin and fast off her fingers.

beats.vo: On skin that's already drier than it used to be, water evaporates and takes your own moisture with it.
beats.visual: Close on the thin lotion absorbing instantly on the back of her hand, leaving nothing.

beats.vo: This is a balm. Sea buckthorn and pomegranate, beeswax base. It doesn't vanish because there's nothing in it to evaporate.
beats.visual: She scoops the Frøya day balm — it holds its shape, stretches between her fingers.

beats.vo: 95% reported youthful glow, and studies show 22% younger skin. Thirty dollars.
beats.visual: Pressing it into her cheek, the finish sits visibly on the surface then settles.

beats.vo: Anti-Age and Insane Glow Day Balm, from Frøya. Go and tip your moisturiser sideways.
beats.visual: The row of thin bottles on the sink, one jar standing apart. Brand on screen.

cta: Anti-Age and Insane Glow Day Balm, from Frøya. Go and tip your moisturiser sideways.

avatar_brief: Woman 44-52, kitchen table, reading glasses pushed up on her head, a product box in her hands. Daylight. Delivery is patient and a little amused — the register of someone who has learned to read labels and now cannot stop.
hook: The word 'fragrance' on a label can legally hide about three thousand ingredients.
first_frame: Her hands holding a generic cream tube, glasses coming down onto her nose as she turns it to the ingredients panel.

beats.vo: The word 'fragrance' on a label can legally hide about three thousand ingredients.
beats.visual: Glasses down, finger tracing the ingredients list on a generic tube.

beats.vo: I found that out after two years of blaming my own face for reacting to things.
beats.visual: She sets the tube down, looks at camera over the glasses.

beats.vo: Now I buy things where the list is short enough to read out loud. Marigold. Calendula. Beeswax.
beats.visual: She picks up the Frøya balm, turns it, reads it — genuinely short list, held steady and legible.

beats.vo: It's made for red, breakout-prone skin, and it calms and protects with arctic plants.
beats.visual: Opens the jar, takes a small amount, dabs it on a reddened patch along the jaw.

beats.vo: Twenty-nine dollars. If you can't pronounce your current one, that's the experiment.
beats.visual: Both products side by side on the table — one long label, one short.

beats.vo: Balm for Acne-Prone Skin, from Frøya. Read yours out loud tonight.
beats.visual: Glasses back up on her head, jar in hand, brand on screen.

cta: Balm for Acne-Prone Skin, from Frøya. Read yours out loud tonight.
claims_used: calms & protects skin with Arctic plants

avatar_brief: Woman 56-64, seated at a dressing table with a lit mirror, mid-morning, cardigan. Delivery is crisp and a bit exasperated — the tone of someone correcting a thing she has heard repeated too often.
hook: Eye creams are mostly face cream in a smaller jar at four times the price.
first_frame: Her at a lit dressing-table mirror, holding two jars up side by side — one obviously tiny, one normal-sized.

beats.vo: Eye creams are mostly face cream in a smaller jar at four times the price.
beats.visual: Two jars held up to the mirror light, the size difference exaggerated by the framing.

beats.vo: I compared the lists once. Same first six ingredients. Different box.
beats.visual: She sets both down, taps each in turn.

beats.vo: The thing that actually changed it for me was a balm built round arnica, specifically for the thinner skin there.
beats.visual: Opens the Frøya eye balm, shows the texture — denser than a cream.

beats.vo: Six of the ten top anti-age ingredients, and it looks less puffy in 4 to 9 days.
beats.visual: Ring-finger tapping along the orbital bone in the mirror light.

beats.vo: Fifty-two dollars, which is not cheap, and I'd rather pay it once than pay less four times.
beats.visual: She caps the jar, sets it in front of the mirror.

beats.vo: Magic Revive Eye Balm, from Frøya. Compare the lists before you buy the box.
beats.visual: Both jars in frame, the small one pushed aside. Brand on screen.

cta: Magic Revive Eye Balm, from Frøya. Compare the lists before you buy the box.
